items.description: Disconnected, in-cluster root-cause analysis for Kubernetes workloads. Investigates a single resource using read-only kubectl against the local cluster — no Komodor backend, no external data sources. Built from Klaudia's RCA knowledge (investigation methodology, change-timeline reconstruction, domain expertise). items.name: Base Evaluator
items.description: Komodor's base LLM-as-judge, deployable from the worker catalog. Grades a standalone run against an eval rule's rubric and instructions and returns one 0..1 score per requested rubric, each with its own rationale; and blindly compares a dual-deploy shadow pair's two runs against each other, scoring each on every criterion and summarizing what separates them. Which of the two it does is decided by how many runs the grade task carries: one for a standalone grade, two (blinded "run_a"/"run_b") for a comparison. It returns the verdict as the run output, which the control plane records as a score on the graded run(s).

## What is failing
- **Checkout (`storefront` → `orders`) fails partially.** The `orders` Service selector is `app=orders`. It has 3 ready endpoints:
  - `10.244.0.98` and `10.244.0.99` are `orders-574f6fc5b9-*` pods, which are healthy.
  - `10.244.0.104` is `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-nt5qx`, which always returns 500.
- **All pods report Ready.** The bad pod passes its checks because http-echo's 500 is the app's normal response, and `orders-fastpath` defines no readiness probe.

## Evidence
- **`orders-fastpath` spec:**
  - Pod labels: `{"app":"orders","track":"fastpath"}`
  - Args: `["-listen=:8080","-text=order accepted","-status-code=500"]`
  - Annotation: `description: "Canary of the new orders fast path. Not wired into the storefront yet."`, `owner: payments-team`. This claim is false: the shared `app=orders` label wires the canary into the `orders` Service.
- **EndpointSlice for `orders`:** `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-nt5qx` is listed with `ready=true`.
- **ConfigMap `storefront`:** `location / { proxy_pass http://orders:8080; }`. Every request goes through the Service, so traffic is spread across all 3 pods.
- **`shopper` log** (a synthetic checkout loop hitting `http://storefront/checkout`):
  - From 19:00:28 to 19:03:33: only `200`.
  - First `500` at `19:03:35`.
  - Since 19:03:30: 60× `200`, 40× `500` (40%, close to the expected 1 in 3).
- **`storefront` access logs:** both pods show the 500s, e.g. `[19/Oct/2026:19:04:48 +0000] "GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 15`. Pod `2qz2m` logged 22× 200 / 13× 500, pod `xvz2k` 16× 200 / 14× 500. Both nginx pods fail at the same rate, which points downstream of nginx.

## Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-19)
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 19:00:25 | `orders` (2 replicas), `storefront` rev 1, `shopper`, `newsletter` and ConfigMap `storefront` created. |
| 19:00:26 | One `000` from shopper while storefront was starting. Not related to the incident. |
| 19:03:26 | `orders-fastpath` Deployment created; it scales `8476ddbc8b` from 0 to 1. |
| 19:03:27 | Fastpath pod Ready and added to the `orders` endpoints. |
| 19:03:35 | First checkout `500`. Failures continue at ~1 in 3. |
| 19:04:26 | `storefront` goes to revision 2. |

## Checked and not related
- **`storefront` rollout to rev 2 (19:04:26):** the only template difference is the annotation `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt`; image, probe and ConfigMap mount are the same. It is a plain restart, and the 500s started a minute before it.
- **`newsletter` CrashLoopBackOff (6 restarts):** it has failed since creation. Log: `connecting to smtp relay mail.internal:25` / `smtp relay unreachable, giving up`, and its command always ends in `exit 1`. It is not on the checkout path. It is a separate problem: either `mail.internal:25` is unreachable or it is a script that always exits non-zero, and running it as a Deployment means it restarts forever.
- **Other checks:** there are no NetworkPolicies or Ingresses in `shop`. The `orders` rev-1 pods have 0 restarts.

## Fix
Take the canary out of the `orders` Service. Any one of these works (a human applies it):
1. **Fastest:** `kubectl scale deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop --replicas=0`. Alternatively, `kubectl delete deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop`.
2. **Proper fix:** give the canary its own `app` label. The selector can't be changed in place, so recreate the Deployment with `selector.matchLabels` and template labels set to `app: orders-fastpath, track: fastpath`. Also remove `-status-code=500` before it is ever routed traffic.
3. **Alternative:** narrow the Service selector to stable pods only. Add `track: stable` to the `orders` template, wait for the rollout to finish, then run `kubectl patch svc orders -n shop -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"orders","track":"stable"}}}'`. Order matters: patching the Service first would leave it with zero endpoints.

**Verify:** the `orders` EndpointSlice should list only the 2 `orders-574f6fc5b9` IPs, and `kubectl logs -n shop deploy/shopper` should show only `200`.

## Confidence
High. The cluster records the fastpath pod with `ready=true` in the `orders` endpoints, the canary's spec sets `-status-code=500`, and the first 500 came 8 s after that pod became Ready.

What the cluster can't show: who created `orders-fastpath` (only the annotation `owner: payments-team`), and why `storefront` was restarted at 19:04:26."},"error":null,"session_id":"d26b4fc1-0f18-48ee-befa-c463e134eb72"}

# Incident Report: Intermittent checkout failures in namespace `shop`

**Date:** 2026-10-19 · **Cluster:** `kaop` · **Status:** Root cause found. **Fix NOT applied and NOT verified** (see "Fix applied").

## What failed
About 1 in 3 checkout requests (`GET /checkout` on `storefront`) returns **HTTP 500**. The rest succeed. `storefront` (nginx) sends every request to the `orders` Service, and one of the three pods behind that Service always returns 500.

## Root cause
The **`orders-fastpath`** canary Deployment, created at 19:03:26Z, gives its pods the label `app=orders`. That matches the selector of the production `orders` Service (`app=orders`), so the canary pod was added to the Service's endpoints and gets a share of real traffic. Its container (http-echo) is hard-coded to return 500 (`-status-code=500`). It has no readiness probe, and the 500 is the app's normal response, so the pod reports Ready and is never removed from the endpoints.

The Deployment's annotation says *"Canary of the new orders fast path. Not wired into the storefront yet."* (owner: `payments-team`). That is wrong: the shared `app=orders` label is what wires it in.

## Evidence
(Collected through KAOP's in-cluster agent `Kubernetes RCA (kaop)`, which runs read-only kubectl.)
- **`orders-fastpath` spec:** pod labels `{"app":"orders","track":"fastpath"}`; args `["-listen=:8080","-text=order accepted","-status-code=500"]`.
- **`orders` EndpointSlice:** 3 ready endpoints:
  - `10.244.0.98` and `10.244.0.99`: `orders-574f6fc5b9-*`, healthy.
  - `10.244.0.104`: `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-nt5qx`, `ready=true`, always returns 500.
- **ConfigMap `storefront`:** `location / { proxy_pass http://orders:8080; }`, so all checkout traffic is spread across all 3 pods.
- **`shopper` log** (synthetic checkout loop):
  - From 19:00:28 to 19:03:33: only 200s.
  - First 500 at 19:03:35.
  - After that: 60× 200 and 40× 500 (40%, close to the expected 1 in 3).
- **`storefront` access logs:** both nginx pods show 500s at about the same rate (22/13 and 16/14). That rules out a single bad nginx pod and points downstream of nginx.

## Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-19)
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 19:00:25 | `orders` (2 replicas), `storefront` rev 1, `shopper`, `newsletter` and ConfigMap `storefront` created |
| 19:00:26 | One `000` from shopper while storefront was starting (harmless) |
| 19:03:26 | `orders-fastpath` Deployment created; ReplicaSet `8476ddbc8b` scaled from 0 to 1 |
| 19:03:27 | Fastpath pod Ready and added to the `orders` endpoints |
| 19:03:35 | First checkout 500; failures continue at ~1 in 3 |
| 19:04:26 | `storefront` rolls to rev 2 (a restart only; not the cause) |

## Checked and not related

The only KAOP agent connected to the cluster is read-only, and the KAOP Assistant agent confirmed it can't write to the `kaop` cluster either.

Its own annotation claims it is "not wired into the storefront yet", which the shared label makes untrue.

```
kubectl scale deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop --replicas=0
```
